title: Sound Walls & Resilient Channel
short_answer: Batt in the cavity is not a sound wall by itself.
summary: Batt in the cavity is not a sound wall by itself.
plain_words: Batt in the cavity is not a sound wall by itself. Seal what the detail calls for, offset boxes when you can, and if drawings show resilient channel or isolation clips, install them so board screws do not hit the stud through the channel. Wrong attach = failed acoustics and tear-out.
when_to_use: When the job calls for sound walls & resilient channel
prerequisites: Read drawings and finish schedule before acting

steps.title: Read the wall type / STC note on the partition schedule
steps.body: do not copy the last job's channel spacing.

steps.title: Insulation + perimeter seal per Insulation / sou
steps.body: Insulation + perimeter seal per Insulation / sound-wall guidance before the second side closes.

steps.title: RC / hat channel / clips: orientation and fasten
steps.body: RC / hat channel / clips: orientation and fastening per the manufacturer and the listed assembly — not memory.

steps.title: Screw length trap: fasteners into the channel on
steps.body: Screw length trap: fasteners into the channel only where required; screws that bite the stud through RC short-circuit the decoupling.

steps.title: Boxes and penetrations
steps.body: back-to-back boxes are acoustic holes; offset or seal per detail.

steps.title: Wall vs plenum: STC wall stopped at a suspended
steps.body: Wall vs plenum: STC wall stopped at a suspended ceiling with open plenum above — ask before hang (same rule as Insulation Full detail).

steps.body: Photo channel / clip layout before board when it is a hold point (Inspection Photos).
